subproblems.title: Derivative lower bound from a lower Lipschitz bound at a point (step 1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, U ⊆ ℝ^n an open set, a ∈ U and m ∈ ℝ. Suppose g is differentiable at a and m|x − a| ≤ |g(x) − g(a)| for every x ∈ U. Then m|v| ≤ |Dg(a)v| for every v ∈ ℝ^n, where Dg(a) = fderiv ℝ g a.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (a : Euclid n) (m : ℝ), IsOpen U → a ∈ U → DifferentiableAt ℝ g a → (∀ x ∈ U, m * ‖x - a‖ ≤ ‖g x - g a‖) → ∀ v : Euclid n, m * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ g a v‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 1 of the parent proof: 'Let a ∈ B and v ∈ ℝ^n. Since B is open, a + tv ∈ B for small t > 0, and then mt|v| ≤ |g(a + tv) − g(a)|. Dividing by t and letting t ↓ 0 gives m|v| ≤ |Dg(a)v|.' Here the open ball B is replaced by the open set U, and the two-point lower bound is needed only with base point a.
Notation: L := Dg(a) = fderiv ℝ g a. For t ≠ 0, q(t) := t^{-1}(g(a + tv) − g(a)).

1. (Difference quotients converge.)
- Fix v ∈ ℝ^n. Since g is differentiable at a with derivative L, g(a + w) − g(a) − Lw = o(|w|) as w → 0.
- Take w = tv with t > 0 and t → 0. Then q(t) − Lv = t^{-1}(g(a + tv) − g(a) − L(tv)) → 0. (If v = 0 this is trivial, since then q(t) = 0 = Lv.)
- Hence q(t) → Lv as t ↓ 0, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0.
- In Mathlib this is HasFDerivAt.lim with c(t) = t^{-1}. Here |c(t)| → ∞ along 𝓝[>] 0 by tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero and tendsto_norm_atTop_atTop. Also c(t)(g(a + c(t)^{-1}v) − g(a)) = q(t), because (t^{-1})^{-1} = t.

2. (Points of U.) Since U is open and a ∈ U, U is a neighbourhood of a. The map t ↦ a + tv is continuous and equals a at t = 0. So a + tv ∈ U for all t in a neighbourhood of 0, and in particular eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.

3. (Inequality for small t.)
- Let t > 0 with a + tv ∈ U. By step 2 this holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and t > 0 holds on 𝓝[>] 0 by definition.
- The hypothesis with x = a + tv gives m|(a + tv) − a| ≤ |g(a + tv) − g(a)|.
- Since (a + tv) − a = tv and |tv| = t|v|, this reads t·(m|v|) ≤ |g(a + tv) − g(a)|.
- Dividing by t > 0 gives m|v| ≤ t^{-1}|g(a + tv) − g(a)| = |q(t)|, using |t^{-1}| = t^{-1}.

4. (Passage to the limit.)
- By step 1 and continuity of the norm, |q(t)| → |Lv| along 𝓝[>] 0.
- The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, and by step 3 the inequality m|v| ≤ |q(t)| holds eventually along it.
- The set {y ∈ ℝ : m|v| ≤ y} is closed, so the limit satisfies m|v| ≤ |Lv| (Mathlib: ge_of_tendsto).
- Since v was arbitrary, m|v| ≤ |Dg(a)v| for every v ∈ ℝ^n. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). Mathlib alone suffices. Useful names: HasFDerivAt.lim (with hg.hasFDerivAt and simpa only [inv_inv]), tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero, tendsto_norm_atTop_atTop, Tendsto.norm, IsOpen.mem_nhds, nhdsWithin_le_nhds, self_mem_nhdsWithin, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg, le_inv_mul_iff₀, ge_of_tendsto.
proof_key_steps: Differentiability of g at a gives t^{-1}(g(a + tv) − g(a)) → Dg(a)v as t ↓ 0.
Since U is open, a + tv ∈ U for small t > 0. Then t·m|v| ≤ |g(a + tv) − g(a)|, i.e. m|v| ≤ |t^{-1}(g(a + tv) − g(a))|.
Let t ↓ 0 along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0. The non-strict inequality passes to the limit: m|v| ≤ |Dg(a)v|.

subproblems.title: Area formula for the blow-ups of an injective regular image (step 3)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, B ⊆ ℝ^n a Borel set, z ∈ ℝ^n, s > 0 and f : ℝ^P → ℝ an arbitrary function. Assume g is differentiable at every a ∈ B, g is injective on B, and Dg(a) is injective for every a ∈ B. Notation:
- B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B}.
- η_{w,s}(y) := s^{-1}(y − w) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).
- J(a) := √det(Dg(a)* ∘ Dg(a)), where Dg(a)* is the adjoint; this is Simon's Jacobian J_g, Ch. 2 (3.3).
Then ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(g(B))} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z + sb) · f(s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z))) dL^n(b). Here H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P and L^n is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n. Both sides are Bochner integrals, with value 0 for non-integrable integrands.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (z : Euclid n) (s : ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), MeasurableSet B → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ g a) → InjOn g B → (∀ a ∈ B, Injective (fderiv ℝ g a)) → 0 < s → ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap (g z) s '' (g '' B), f y ∂μHE[n] = ∫ b in {b : Euclid n | z + s • b ∈ B}, Real.sqrt (((fderiv ℝ g (z + s • b)).adjoint ∘L fderiv ℝ g (z + s • b)).det) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 3 of the parent proof. It applies the area formula for injective maps with injective derivative to the rescaled map φ_s: Simon Ch. 2, §3, (3.2), with the weighted form (3.5). In SimonGMT this is the Bochner identity Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, valid for every integrand. Here B is an arbitrary Borel set (the parent uses B = B_r(c)), and z need not lie in B.
Notation: w := g(z); φ(b) := s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − w); B_s := {b : z + sb ∈ B}.

1. (B_s is Borel.) The affine map b ↦ z + sb is continuous, hence Borel measurable. B_s is the preimage of the Borel set B under this map, so B_s is measurable.

2. (Derivative of φ.)
- Let b ∈ B_s and a := z + sb ∈ B, so g is differentiable at a.
- The map b' ↦ z + sb' has derivative s·id at b. By the chain rule, b' ↦ g(z + sb') has derivative Dg(a) ∘ (s·id) at b.
- Subtracting the constant w leaves the derivative unchanged; multiplying by the scalar s^{-1} multiplies it by s^{-1}. So φ is differentiable at b with Dφ(b) = s^{-1}·(Dg(a) ∘ (s·id)).
- For every v, s^{-1}·Dg(a)(sv) = s^{-1}s·Dg(a)v = Dg(a)v, by linearity and s ≠ 0.
- Hence Dφ(b) = Dg(z + sb). It is injective by hypothesis, since z + sb ∈ B.

3. (φ is injective on B_s.) Let b, b' ∈ B_s with φ(b) = φ(b'). Multiplying by s gives g(z + sb) − w = g(z + sb') − w, so g(z + sb) = g(z + sb'). Both z + sb and z + sb' lie in B, and g is injective on B, so z + sb = z + sb'. Hence sb = sb', and b = b' because s ≠ 0.

4. (φ(B_s) = η_{w,s}(g(B)).)
- If b ∈ B_s, then φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − w) = η_{w,s}(g(z + sb)) with z + sb ∈ B. So φ(b) ∈ η_{w,s}(g(B)).
- Conversely, let y = η_{w,s}(g(a)) with a ∈ B, and put b := s^{-1}(a − z). Then z + sb = z + (a − z) = a ∈ B, so b ∈ B_s, and φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(a) − w) = y.

5. (Area formula.) Let E = ℝ^n and F = ℝ^P. By steps 1–3:
- B_s is measurable;
- φ is differentiable at each point of B_s with injective derivative;
- φ is injective on B_s.
The Bochner area formula therefore gives, for the function f, ∫_{φ(B_s)} f dμHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫_{B_s} J_φ(b) f(φ(b)) dμHE[finrank ℝ E](b). No integrability is needed: both sides are Bochner integrals and the formula is an identity for every integrand. Here J_φ(b) := √det(Dφ(b)* ∘ Dφ(b)) is the metric Jacobian of φ. This is SimonGMT's areaJacobianAt φ b, which equals the square root by areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp.

6. (Normalisation.) finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, so both measures are μHE[n]. On ℝ^n, μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure L^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By step 4, the left side is ∫_{η_{w,s}(g(B))} f dH^n.

7. (Jacobian.)
- For b ∈ B_s, step 2 gives Dφ(b) = Dg(z + sb). Hence J_φ(b) = √det(Dg(z + sb)* ∘ Dg(z + sb)) = J(z + sb), and φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)).
- B_s is measurable, so the integrand on the right may be replaced on B_s (setIntegral_congr_fun).
- This gives ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(g(B))} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z + sb) f(s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z))) dL^n(b). ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). Add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea`; it is prebuilt and already imported by accepted DAG nodes.
- Apply Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (E := Euclid n) (F := Euclid P) (G := ℝ) to φ := fun b => s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z) on {b | z + s • b ∈ B}.
- Prove `HasFDerivAt φ (fderiv ℝ g (z + s • b)) b` from (((hdiff _ hb).hasFDerivAt.comp b h1).sub_const (g z)).const_smul s⁻¹, where h1 := ((hasFDerivAt_id b).const_smul s).const_add z. Finish with HasFDerivAt.congr_fderiv and ContinuousLinearMap.ext, using map_smul, smul_smul and inv_mul_cancel₀.
- Rewrite the image, then finrank_euclideanSpace_fin and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n.
- On B_s, rewrite Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp and the derivative identity before unfolding φ; then use smul_eq_mul.
proof_key_steps: B_s = {b : z + sb ∈ B} is Borel. φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)) is differentiable on B_s with Dφ(b) = Dg(z + sb), which is injective.
φ is injective on B_s (g is injective on B and s ≠ 0), and φ(B_s) = η_{g(z),s}(g(B)), using b = s^{-1}(a − z).
The Bochner area formula for φ on B_s gives ∫_{φ(B_s)} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J_φ · (f∘φ) dH^n.
Since finrank ℝ^n = n, H^n = L^n on ℝ^n, and J_φ(b) = √det(Dg(z+sb)*Dg(z+sb)) on B_s, the identity follows.

subproblems.title: Linear area formula in integral form (step 7)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P an injective (continuous) linear map, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ an arbitrary function. Then ∫_{L(ℝ^n)} f dH^n = √det(L* ∘ L) · ∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lb) dL^n(b). Here L(ℝ^n) is the range submodule of L viewed as a set, L* is the adjoint, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, and L^n is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n. Both integrals are Bochner integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), Injective L → ∫ y in (LinearMap.range (L : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) : Set (Euclid P)), f y ∂μHE[n] = Real.sqrt ((L.adjoint ∘L L).det) * ∫ b, f (L b)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 7 of the parent proof: 'apply the area formula of step 3 to the injective linear map L on ℝ^n. Its derivative is L at every point, so its Jacobian is J_L … and L(ℝ^n) = T.' This is Simon Ch. 2, §3, (3.1) in integral form: H^n(ℓ(A)) = √det(ℓ*∘ℓ) H^n(A) for linear ℓ : ℝ^n → ℝ^{n+k}. It is obtained from the Bochner area formula, SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative.

1. (Hypotheses of the area formula.) Take the source set s = ℝ^n, which is measurable. A continuous linear map is differentiable everywhere and is its own derivative: DL(x) = L for every x (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv). Hence DL(x) is injective for every x by hypothesis, and L is injective on ℝ^n.

2. (Area formula.) The Bochner area formula, an identity valid for every integrand, gives ∫_{L(ℝ^n)} f dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] = ∫_{ℝ^n} J_L(x) f(Lx) dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n](x). Here J_L(x) = √det(DL(x)* ∘ DL(x)): SimonGMT's areaJacobianAt L x, rewritten by areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp. By step 1, J_L(x) = √det(L* ∘ L) for every x, a constant.

3. (Normalisation.) finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, so both measures are μHE[n]. On ℝ^n, μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). The restriction of a measure to the whole space is the measure itself. So the right side is ∫_{ℝ^n} √det(L*∘L)·f(Lx) dL^n(x).

4. (Image.) L(ℝ^n) = range L. This set is the one underlying the submodule LinearMap.range L (Mathlib LinearMap.coe_range); the coercion of L to a linear map has the same underlying function (ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe).

5. (Constant.) For every integrand φ and constant c, ∫ c·φ = c·∫ φ (integral_const_mul). Indeed, if c ≠ 0 then c·φ is integrable iff φ is, and both sides are 0 in the non-integrable case; if c = 0 both sides are 0. Therefore ∫_{range L} f dH^n = √det(L* ∘ L)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lb) dL^n(b). ∎

subproblems.title: Convergence of the rescaled integrals by localisation and dominated convergence (steps 4–7)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and z ∈ ℝ^n. Let g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be continuous and differentiable at z, h : ℝ^n → ℝ continuous, B ⊆ ℝ^n open with z ∈ B, m > 0, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with compact support. Assume m|a − z| ≤ |g(a) − g(z)| for all a ∈ B, and m|v| ≤ |Dg(z)v| for all v ∈ ℝ^n. Then, as s ↓ 0 (along the filter 𝓝[>] 0),
∫_{B_s} h(z + sb) · f(s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z))) dL^n(b) → h(z) · ∫_{ℝ^n} f(Dg(z)b) dL^n(b),
where B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B} and L^n is Lebesgue measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (z : Euclid n) (m : ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), Continuous g → DifferentiableAt ℝ g z → Continuous h → IsOpen B → z ∈ B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, m * ‖a - z‖ ≤ ‖g a - g z‖) → (∀ v : Euclid n, m * ‖v‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ g z v‖) → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ∫ b in {b : Euclid n | z + s • b ∈ B}, h (z + s • b) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (h z * ∫ b, f (fderiv ℝ g z b)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 4–6 and the first half of step 7 of the parent proof. The continuous Jacobian J_g is replaced by an arbitrary continuous weight h. (The parent applies this with h = J_g, continuous by its step 2, and B = B_r(c).) The hypothesis m|v| ≤ |Dg(z)v| is the conclusion of parent step 1 at z; here it is assumed.
Notation: L := Dg(z) = fderiv ℝ g z. For s > 0:
- B_s := {b : z + sb ∈ B};
- φ_s(b) := s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z));
- F_s(b) := h(z + sb)·f(φ_s(b));
- I(s) := ∫_{B_s} F_s dL^n.

1. (Radius R for f.) The support of f is compact, hence bounded: tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ. Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. If |y| > R then f(y) = 0: otherwise y ∈ tsupport f, so |y| ≤ R₀ ≤ R, a contradiction.

2. (Radius ρ₀.) B is open and z ∈ B, so there is ε > 0 with the open ball B_ε(z) ⊆ B. Put ρ₀ := ε/2 > 0. Then closedBall(z, ρ₀) ⊆ B_ε(z) ⊆ B.

3. (The compact set K.) Put K := closedBall(0, R/m) ⊆ ℝ^n and s₀ := mρ₀/R > 0.
(a) Let 0 < s ≤ s₀ and b ∈ K. Then |(z + sb) − z| = s|b| ≤ s₀·(R/m) = ρ₀, so z + sb ∈ closedBall(z, ρ₀) ⊆ B. In particular K ⊆ B_s.
(b) Let s > 0 and b ∈ B_s ∖ K. Then |b| > R/m, so m|b| > R (as m > 0). Since a := z + sb ∈ B, the hypothesis gives m·s|b| = m|a − z| ≤ |g(z + sb) − g(z)|. Hence |φ_s(b)| = s^{-1}|g(z + sb) − g(z)| ≥ m|b| > R. By step 1, f(φ_s(b)) = 0, so F_s(b) = 0.

4. (Localisation.) The condition 0 < s < s₀ holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. For such s:
- B_s is open, being the preimage of the open set B under the continuous map b ↦ z + sb; hence it is measurable;
- K ⊆ B_s by 3(a);
- F_s = 0 on B_s ∖ K by 3(b).
Therefore ∫_{B_s} F_s dL^n = ∫_K F_s dL^n (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero). So I(s) = ∫_K F_s dL^n eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.

5. (Uniform bound.)
- h is continuous on the compact set closedBall(z, ρ₀), so |h(a)| ≤ Λ for some Λ and all a ∈ closedBall(z, ρ₀).
- f is continuous with compact support, so |f(y)| ≤ C for some C and all y.
- For 0 < s < s₀ and b ∈ K, step 3(a) gives z + sb ∈ closedBall(z, ρ₀), hence |F_s(b)| ≤ ΛC.
- The constant ΛC is integrable on K because L^n(K) < ∞ (closed balls have finite Lebesgue measure).

6. (Measurability.) For each s, b ↦ F_s(b) is continuous. It is built from the continuous maps g, h and f, the affine map b ↦ z + sb, subtraction of the constant g(z), multiplication by s^{-1}, and a product of real functions. Hence it is a.e.-strongly measurable for L^n restricted to K.

7. (Pointwise limit.) Fix b ∈ ℝ^n.
- g is differentiable at z, so φ_s(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)) → Lb as s ↓ 0: this is the difference quotient in the direction b. In Mathlib use HasFDerivAt.lim with c(s) = s^{-1}, since |s^{-1}| → ∞ along 𝓝[>] 0.
- z + sb → z as s → 0, so h(z + sb) → h(z) by continuity of h.
- f(φ_s(b)) → f(Lb) by continuity of f.
Hence F_s(b) → h(z)·f(Lb).

8. (Dominated convergence.)
- The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is countably generated.
- Steps 5–7 verify the hypotheses of dominated convergence along a filter (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) for L^n restricted to K, with bound ΛC.
- Hence ∫_K F_s dL^n → ∫_K h(z) f(Lb) dL^n(b) as s ↓ 0.
- By step 4, s ↦ I(s) and s ↦ ∫_K F_s agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. So I(s) → ∫_K h(z) f(Lb) dL^n(b).

9. (Identification of the limit.)
- If b ∉ K then |b| > R/m, so R < m|b| ≤ |Lb| by the hypothesis on L, and f(Lb) = 0 by step 1.
- Hence ∫_K h(z) f(Lb) db = ∫_{ℝ^n} h(z) f(Lb) db (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero) = h(z)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lb) db (integral_const_mul).
- Therefore I(s) → h(z)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Dg(z)b) dL^n(b) as s ↓ 0. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). Mathlib alone suffices. Useful names:
- Radius R: HasCompactSupport.isCompact, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall, subset_tsupport.
- Radius ρ₀: Metric.isOpen_iff, closedBall_subset_ball.
- Localisation: setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, with IsOpen.preimage and IsOpen.measurableSet for B_s.
- Bounds: IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn, Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support.
- Dominated convergence: tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence (fun _ => Λ * C), integrableOn_const with measure_closedBall_lt_top, ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_closedBall, Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable.
- Pointwise limit: HasFDerivAt.lim with tendsto_norm_atTop_atTop.comp tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero and simpa only [inv_inv]; Tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds.
- Identification and conclusion: setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, integral_const_mul, Tendsto.congr'.
proof_key_steps: Choose R > 0 with f = 0 off closedBall(0, R) and ρ₀ > 0 with closedBall(z, ρ₀) ⊆ B. Set K = closedBall(0, R/m) and s₀ = mρ₀/R.
For 0 < s ≤ s₀, K ⊆ B_s, and the integrand vanishes on B_s ∖ K because |φ_s(b)| ≥ m|b| > R. So I(s) = ∫_K F_s.
On K, F_s is continuous and |F_s| ≤ Λ·sup|f|, where Λ = max of |h| on closedBall(z, ρ₀). Pointwise F_s(b) → h(z) f(Dg(z)b), so dominated convergence along 𝓝[>] 0 gives ∫_K F_s → ∫_K h(z) f(Dg(z)b).
Off K, f(Dg(z)b) = 0 since |Dg(z)b| ≥ m|b| > R. So the limit equals h(z)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Dg(z)b) db.
